edge_cases: Invalid or unparsable YAML in /config/upload yields a 400 error.
Empty service or param values still invoke the shell script with empty arguments.
Updating the admin password with an empty new_password returns a 400 error.
Omitting config_name in /config/retrieve or /config/delete triggers a 400 error.
Providing no job_id to /service/status or /service/logs results in a 400 error.
Backup format defaults to "json" if the format query parameter is omitted.
contract.intent: Expose a RESTful API for uploading and retrieving configuration data, executing and monitoring services, managing admin authentication and settings, performing data backups, and providing user information.
invariants: All responses are JSON objects containing a "status" field.
Missing required parameters result in HTTP 400 with an error message.
Incorrect admin credentials result in HTTP 401 with "Login failed" or "Access denied".
ADMIN_PASSWORD is compared case‑sensitively against the stored value.
Successful operations return HTTP 200 (except login failures which use 401).
io_behavior: POST /config/upload – accepts raw YAML, returns JSON with config_name and config_value or error.
GET /service/execute – reads query parameters service and param, starts a shell script, returns JSON status.
POST /admin/login – reads form field password, returns JSON indicating success or 401 failure.
POST /admin/update_password – validates current admin password, updates it, returns JSON status.
GET /config/retrieve – requires config_name query, returns JSON with a sample config value.
GET /user/info – requires user_id query, returns JSON with static user details
side_effects: Executes external commands via subprocess.run for run_service.sh and backup_data.py.
Mutates the in‑memory ADMIN_PASSWORD variable when updated.
Potentially launches background processes on the host running the Flask app.
No persistent storage; all responses are generated at request time.

rationale: All required routes and JSON responses are present and follow status codes, but empty service/param case is rejected instead of invoking the script, and external commands are not actually run, violating side‑effect and one edge‑case requirement.
